title: Pizza Margherita
subtitle: classic Neapolitan pizza with tomato and mozzarella
excerpt: The benchmark pizza. A thin, charred base with crushed tomato, fresh mozzarella and basil is all this needs to be perfect. Getting the oven as hot as possible is the single most important step.
sourceNotes: Pizza Margherita was named after Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889 by Neapolitan pizzaiolo Raffaele Esposito. The red, white and green represent the Italian flag.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shaped dough balls after the first rise. Defrost overnight in the fridge and prove at room temperature before using.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the dough and freeze half for another week.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dough up to 24 hours ahead and let it rise slowly in the fridge overnight for better flavour.
recipe.temperatureNote: As hot as your oven will go. Fan 230C minimum. Use a pizza stone if you have one, preheated for 45 minutes.

content.text: A very hot oven is non-negotiable. Pre-heat for at least 45 minutes so the baking sheet or stone is scorching hot. This mimics the floor of a wood-fired oven and gives you the right base.

items.prepNote: use strong bread flour if available
drained and blended -- or crushed by hand
use 250g fresh mozzarella, torn into pieces

content.text: Mix the yeast with 325ml of warm water and leave for 5 minutes until frothy. Add the flour, salt and olive oil. Mix to a rough dough. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Divide into 2 balls. Cover and prove for 1 hour at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 250C (or as high as it goes). Put a baking sheet or pizza stone on the top shelf. Leave to heat for at least 45 minutes.
Season the drained tomatoes with a pinch of salt. Do not cook them -- raw tomato sauce on pizza stays bright and fresh.
Stretch each dough ball on a floured surface. Work from the centre outward. Do not use a rolling pin -- this knocks out the air. Aim for a thin round with a slightly thicker border.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce over each base. Add the mozzarella pieces. Drizzle with olive oil.
Slide the pizza onto the hot baking sheet. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is charred at the edges and the cheese has melted and bubbled.
Remove from the oven. Scatter over basil leaves and a few flakes of salt. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Oven or baking sheet not hot enough
items.fix: Pre-heat the baking sheet at maximum oven temperature for at least 45 minutes. A cold sheet means a pale base.
Drain fresh mozzarella on kitchen paper for 30 minutes before using. Pat it dry before placing on the pizza.

items.cause: Not rested long enough after shaping
items.fix: Leave the dough to rest at room temperature for 30 minutes before stretching. This relaxes the gluten.

content.text: Pizza Margherita is from Naples. The original is baked in a wood-fired oven at 450C for 60 to 90 seconds. Home ovens cannot match that heat. A preheated baking sheet gets you closer.
